title: Collapsed pad swallows note-handle clicks; composer draft bleeds across cards
body:
## Summary
Once the sticky pad is collapsed, clicking any track id (NoteHandle) on Coverage, Spend or Tracks does nothing visible: the composer is only rendered inside the pad's `open &&` block. The collapsed header also hides whether a recalibration is running or a candidate is waiting. Separately, the composer has no `key`, so text typed for one card stays in the field when another card's handle is clicked, and Enter files it against the wrong card.

## Description
StickyNotebook.tsx:58 keeps `open` as local state, default true. ScriptStep.tsx:421-428 records that the pad mounts once so a collapsed pad STAYS collapsed across tabs, which makes collapsed a normal state. In that state NotesContext.tsx:64 `ctx.toggle(cardId)` sets `active`, but StickyNotebook.tsx:95-99 renders `<NoteComposer>` only inside `{open && (...)}` (line 80). The only feedback is the handle's cyan tint. The collapsed header (line 76) reads `notes · N` and nothing else, so `recalibrating` and the staged candidate's accept/discard bar (RecalibrateControl, line 102) are hidden too. The result of a minutes-long paid run can wait unseen.
NoteComposer.tsx:17 `useState("")` lives in an instance that StickyNotebook.tsx:97 reuses for every `cardId`, because it has no `key`.

## Flow
- Collapse the pad (pad-toggle) → open Coverage → click `note-handle-<id>` → handle tints cyan, no composer appears.
- Pad open: type "tighten" in card A's free field → click card B's handle → the field still reads "tighten" → Enter adds it to B.

## Expected impact
The note handle is the step's only way to start a note, and Recalibrate depends on notes. A click that does nothing reads as broken, and a note filed on the wrong card changes the weights a paid recalibration acts on.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - clicking a note handle always shows that card's composer, with an empty draft.
Before: 2 render branches where the click has no visible result or the wrong draft (collapsed pad; card switch with typed text). StickyNotebook.tsx:80 gates the composer and line 97 has no key.
After: 0. The composer renders whenever `ctx.active` is set (opening the pad, or a composer slot outside the `open` gate), `<NoteComposer key={ctx.active} …>`, and the collapsed header carries the running/candidate state as a Tally.
Method: probe - source ratchet on StickyNotebook.tsx
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/script/_notes/StickyNotebook.tsx:58 (useState(true)), :76 (collapsed header = notes count only), :80 ({open && (), :95-99 (composer inside open gate, no key), :102 (RecalibrateControl inside open gate); app/_phases/script/_notes/NotesContext.tsx:64 (toggle only sets active); app/_phases/script/_notes/NoteComposer.tsx:17 (draft state, instance reused across cardId); app/_phases/script/ScriptStep.tsx:421-428 (pad collapse is meant to persist across tabs)
verify: New tests/golden-path/script-sticky-pad.probe.spec.ts reads StickyNotebook.tsx through stripComments and asserts (a) `<NoteComposer` carries `key={ctx.active}` (or `key=`), (b) the `ctx?.active &&` composer branch is not nested only inside the `{open && (` block (e.g. Pad derives `const shown = open || !!ctx?.active`, or opens on active), (c) the collapsed header references `api.running` and `api.candidate`. Red on HEAD, green after. Then npm run typecheck && npm run check:narration (no new prose; any state on the header is a <Tally>).

title: Duel depth keeps the stale paragraph its expert twin turned into StaleBadges
body:
## Summary
The two faces of the Candidates tab show the same rewritten chain but disclose staleness differently. HypothesisColumn uses two `<StaleBadge>`s. CandidatesDuel still prints the ~22-word paragraph those badges replaced, and never marks its hand-typed check counts as not re-run. It also draws those counts as bare glyphs with no spoken label.

## Description
HypothesisColumn.tsx:114-121 is `<StaleBadge words="turns · questions · promise form" …>`. Its comment says this "was a sentence under every one of three columns". HypothesisColumn.tsx:149-153 adds `<StaleBadge words="not re-run">` on the craft checks.
CandidatesDuel.tsx:238-244 renders: "words are counted from X's own chain. Turns, questions aloud and the promise form are the original render's and were not re-measured." That is the same fact in prose, which StaleBadge.tsx:7-10 quotes as the thing it replaced. The duel also renders `VerdictCounts` (line 248), whose `checks: N✓ N! …` row (lines 71-74) comes from the render's hand-typed checks. After a rewrite those counts describe the original chain, and nothing says so. BaselineOnlyNote.tsx:12-17 calls that exact case "manufactures confidence".
The counts are also glyph+colour only (`3✓ 1!`), with no sr-only label. Meters.tsx:64-69 explains why CheckList carries one ("`declared`… vanishes most completely (a bare "!")"). VerdictCounts' header (lines 50-52) claims "the glyphs are Meters' CHECK marks", but it paints unmeasured amber where Meters.tsx:74 paints it white/35.

## Flow
- Accept a model-path recalibration → Candidates, guided face → read more on any card: the paragraph appears, and the checks row shows unmarked ✓/! counts for a chain they were not typed against.
- Switch to full controls: the same facts are two amber badges.

## Expected impact
One staleness concept gets one spelling on both faces. The duel stops implying the hand checks were re-run, and screen-reader users hear "2 pass, 1 declared deviation" rather than "2 check mark 1 exclamation".

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a rewritten chain reads the same on both faces; the check counts are labelled and marked stale.
Before: CandidatesDuel stripped source has 0 `<StaleBadge`, 1 paragraph matching /were not\s+re-measured/, and 0 sr-only labels in VerdictCounts. HypothesisColumn has 2 `<StaleBadge`.
After: CandidatesDuel has 2 `<StaleBadge` (same words/why as HypothesisColumn), 0 matches for the paragraph, and an sr-only label beside each check glyph in VerdictCounts (pass / declared deviation / fail / not measured).
Method: probe - source ratchet comparing the two twins
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/script/candidates/CandidatesDuel.tsx:238-244 (prose paragraph), :71-74 (glyph-only check counts, no sr-only), :50-52 (claims Meters' glyphs; :74 paints unmeasured amber vs Meters.tsx:74 white/35); app/_phases/script/_parts/HypothesisColumn.tsx:114-121,149-153 (the StaleBadge twin); components/ui/signal/StaleBadge.tsx:7-10 (quotes this paragraph as replaced); app/_phases/script/_parts/Meters.tsx:64-75 (why check glyphs need words)
verify: New tests/golden-path/script-candidates-twins.probe.spec.ts: stripComments(CandidatesDuel.tsx) has /were not\s+re-measured/ count 0, `<StaleBadge` count 2 (equal to HypothesisColumn.tsx's count), and `sr-only` occurrences inside VerdictCounts >= 4. Red on HEAD (0 / 1 / 0), green after. npm run typecheck; npm run check:narration unchanged.

title: Tab tallies count whichever version the ACTIVE tab draws, not their own tab's
body:
## Summary
The Tally on each of the four tabs is computed from one `shown` version. That version depends on which tab is active and on the VersionBar toggle. The Tracks tally can therefore count a staged candidate while Tracks always draws the baseline, and the Coverage and Spend tallies change value when you switch to a different tab.

## Description
ScriptStep.tsx:315-316: `comparing = weighing && candidate && showing==="candidate"` and `shown = comparing ? candidate : baseline`, where `weighing` means the ACTIVE tab is coverage or spend. ScriptStep.tsx:326-334 computes conflicts, overrun and unused from `shown` for all four tabs at once, and `tallyFor` (335-343) hands them out. What each tab draws:
- Coverage and Spend draw `shown` while active. While inactive, `shown` falls back to baseline, but clicking the tab draws the candidate (showing defaults to "candidate", line 216).
- Tracks always draws `versions.baseline` (line 496), and MatrixTracks' own gutter reads "in no track · N of M" from the baseline.
So with a candidate staged and Coverage open, the Tracks chip counts the candidate's unused cards and the Tracks tab shows a different N. From Candidates or Tracks, the Coverage chip shows baseline conflicts and opening Coverage draws the candidate's. The code's own comment (322-324) says a tally drawn over the wrong data "is a claim, not a count".

## Flow
- Stage a candidate that brings an unused card in (recalibrate.ts's "new" sentinel path) → on Coverage, the Tracks chip reads UNUSED n-1 → click Tracks → gutter reads n.
- On Candidates, the Coverage chip reads CONFLICT x → click Coverage → the footnote counts the candidate's y.

## Expected impact
Tallies replaced the tab captions so the number could be trusted at a glance. A chip that changes when you click a different tab teaches the reader to ignore it.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - each tab's chip equals the count that tab shows when opened.
Before: 3 of 4 tallies read `shown` (ScriptStep.tsx:328,329,331), which is tab-dependent. The Tracks tally reads a version Tracks never draws.
After: each count reads its own tab's version. Coverage/Spend use `versions.candidate && showing==="candidate" ? candidate : baseline`, independent of the active tab. Tracks uses `versions.baseline`. The stripped source has 0 `(shown,` calls inside `state`.
Method: probe - source ratchet
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/script/ScriptStep.tsx:314-316 (shown depends on active tab), :326-334 (state from shown), :335-343 (tallyFor), :216 (showing defaults to candidate), :496 (Tracks draws versions.baseline); app/_phases/script/_matrix/MatrixTracks.tsx:63,155 (gutter count from baseline)
verify: New tests/golden-path/script-tab-tallies.probe.spec.ts: stripComments(ScriptStep.tsx), slice the `const state = ready` expression, assert it contains no `(shown,`, and that the unused/Tracks count references `versions.baseline`. Red on HEAD (3 `(shown,` calls), green after. npm run typecheck.

title: A failed Research read renders as 'Research not done' with an Open Research CTA
body:
## Summary
Both halves of the Script step decide between UpstreamBreak and the step body with `loadStep(projectId, "research")`. `loadStep` returns the seeded default, usually undefined, when the read FAILS. A storage failure therefore draws as "blocked at Research, go open it" over a project whose research is done: wrong cause, wrong remedy. The sibling Frames step renders a read failure as its own Notice.

## Description
stepStore.ts:563-573 states that a failed read lands as the seeded default, and that "a caller that needs to tell the two apart calls `readStep` instead". ScriptStep.tsx:245-251 (explainer) and :185-190 (music video) call `loadStep` and set `researched = !!saved?.researched`, so failure ≡ false. ScriptStep.tsx:304-312 and :196-204 then render `<UpstreamBreak blockedAt="research" … action="Open Research">`. The music-video half also never reports done, because usePhaseReport (192) waits on `researched`.
The pair: FramesStep.tsx:97-120 renders `ctl.loadTrouble` as a `<Notice>` titled by `kind` (quota / blocked / unavailable) with the store's message verbatim, and the comment says "A STEP THAT COULD NOT BE READ IS NOT AN EMPTY STEP".

## Flow
- IndexedDB read fails (quota, another tab blocking an upgrade, private session) → Script shows the Research node pulsing "missing" and an Open Research button → Research opens with the work intact → back to Script, same picture.

## Expected impact
Failure, empty and loaded each get their own render, and the real error is shown in full (the repo's exemption for errors).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a failed research read is shown as a storage error, not as missing research.
Before: failure and never-researched render the same branch (UpstreamBreak). There are 2 `loadStep(projectId, "research")` call sites in ScriptStep.tsx and 0 `readStep` calls.
After: 2 `readStep` calls, 0 `loadStep(…"research")`. A `trouble` state renders `<Notice severity="error" title={kind}>{message}</Notice>` before the UpstreamBreak branch, mirroring FramesStep.tsx:108-120.
Method: probe - source ratchet
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/_shared/stepStore.ts:563-573 (loadStep flattens failure to seeded default), :302 (ReadOutcome {ok:false; trouble}); app/_phases/script/ScriptStep.tsx:185-190,196-204 (music-video), :245-251,304-312 (explainer); pair app/_phases/frames/FramesStep.tsx:97-120
verify: New tests/golden-path/script-read-failure.probe.spec.ts: stripComments(ScriptStep.tsx) has /loadStep[^;]*"research"/ count 0 and `readStep(` count >= 2, and the index of a `<Notice` keyed to trouble precedes the first `<UpstreamBreak`. Red on HEAD, green after. npm run typecheck; ScriptStep stays in OWN_LOAD_GUARD (shared-notebook-contracts probe green).

title: Locked scope pip is disabled+title: required-why unreachable by keyboard, AT
body:
## Summary
A required card's scope pip (the steel-man) is a `disabled` button whose only explanation is a native `title`. Keyboard users skip it, touch users never see it, and its aria-label says "steel-man is in scope", the same as any untouched card, with nothing about being required. The Coverage conflict marker repeats the pattern. TabRail.tsx:203-206 names this exact regression: "A locked tab is `aria-disabled`, NOT `disabled`… would put the explanation of why it is locked behind a mouse."

## Description
shared.tsx:65 `disabled={locked}` and :66-74 `title={locked ? card.requiredWhy : …}`. :84-90 aria-label covers descoped / not-taken / in-scope only. Visually the locked pip is a faint `text-white/20` tick (:77), so sighted users get no locked mark either. ScopePip renders on every row of Coverage, Spend and Tracks and in the Tracks gutter. MatrixCoverage.tsx:156,180-187: the conflict marker is `disabled` when `card.required`, again with requiredWhy only in `title`.
The other three ScopePip titles (shared.tsx:69-73, e.g. "In scope. Click to descope — the triage board will agree.") narrate the control in sentences of 45+ characters. They pass `npm run check:narration` only because its regex matches `title="literal"` and not `title={expr}` (pipeline/check-narration.mjs:148). That gate blind spot lives outside this context and is noted, not proposed here.

## Flow
- Tab through a Coverage row: focus goes NoteHandle → next row. The steel-man pip is skipped, and its reason ("mandatory (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA §steel_man)…") cannot be reached.
- Screen reader on the pip: "steel-man is in scope, button, dimmed".

## Expected impact
The one card the user is not allowed to cut says so, and why, on every input channel.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the locked pip is focusable, announces "required", and exposes requiredWhy to AT.
Before: 2 controls in this context use `disabled` + title as the only carrier of requiredWhy (shared.tsx:65, MatrixCoverage.tsx:180). The locked aria-label has 0 mention of required.
After: 0 `disabled={locked}`. The locked pip uses `aria-disabled`, keeps its click as a no-op, has aria-label `${id} is required` and `aria-describedby` an sr-only requiredWhy (29 words, over the Hint cap, so not a Hint), and shows a lock mark instead of the faint tick. The conflict marker gets the same treatment for the required case.
Method: probe - source ratchet
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/script/_matrix/shared.tsx:65 (disabled={locked}), :66-74 (title prose, requiredWhy), :77 (faint tick), :84-90 (aria-label omits required); app/_phases/script/_matrix/MatrixCoverage.tsx:156,180-187 (same on conflict marker); app/_phases/_shared/notebook/cards.ts:122-124 (steel-man required, 29-word why); components/ui/signal/TabRail.tsx:203-206 (house rule); pipeline/check-narration.mjs:148 (title regex is literal-only, blind to title={…})
verify: New tests/golden-path/script-scope-pip-a11y.probe.spec.ts: stripComments(shared.tsx) has `disabled={locked}` count 0, `aria-disabled` >= 1, and the aria-label expression contains 'required'. stripComments(MatrixCoverage.tsx) has the conflict button not passing `card.required` into `disabled=`. Red on HEAD, green after. npm run typecheck && npm run check:narration (title count must not rise).

lens_checked.visual-craft: Read all 18 .tsx in the context plus imported Meters.tsx, signal/{StaleBadge,Tally,TabRail,Hint exports}, deck DeckCard/DeckStage usage. Tones are all Tailwind tokens (no hex). Lowest alphas checked: Skeleton bars bg-white/[0.05-0.07] (decorative, aria-hidden), BaselineOnlyNote amber/90, unused cells text-white/25 (labelled '0s'). No Ghost below 40%. Destructive styling: RecalibrateControl 'discard' (:186) and 'clear all' (:250) are neutral one-click. Noted, not emitted: within budget, behind the 5 above.
lens_checked.ux-reviewer: Walked ScriptStep route branches (missing / trailer / music-video / explainer), face switch, the beats Modal from both faces, the VersionBar show-baseline/candidate toggle, the sticky pad open/collapse x NoteHandle x composer (finding 1), and the accept-over-gate arm/confirm (derived armedFor, correct).
lens_checked.state-coverage: Data sources: getProject+research-beats (ScriptStep:132-153), research step (finding 4), useScope/useVersions/useAdoption/useScriptFace hydration (Skeleton until all four), tab tallies (finding 3), DeclinedList (null on zero), StickyNotebook 'no notes yet', MatrixTracks gutter hidden on zero, recalibrate idle/running/candidate/lost/engineNote.
lens_checked.copy-auditor: Diffed comments against JSX in every file. Pairs: HypothesisColumn vs CandidatesDuel (finding 2); GatePanel 'not checked' vs BaselineOnlyNote:79 'untestable' (same gate.unmeasured, two names; below budget); ConstraintLedger:276 plain 'not re-scored' vs StaleBadge 'not re-run' (below budget); VersionBar header 'Candidates… baseline-only' vs ScriptStep:24-30 'CANDIDATES NO LONGER DOES' (code comment only, not rendered). MatrixFootnotes 'gate does not check exclusions yet' verified still true (gate.ts has no scope/exclusion code).
lens_checked.accessibility-checker: TabRail usage (testId/panelId/label), tabpanel without aria-labelledby (minor), PresetSelect combobox/listbox (option hints title-only), NoteComposer free-text input named only by placeholder, VersionBar aria-pressed, GatePanel/ConstraintLedger/CheckList sr-only verdict labels (present), VerdictCounts glyph-only (in finding 2), ScopePip/conflict disabled+title (finding 5), MatrixTracks cross-track glow onMouseEnter only (no focus equivalent), MatrixSpend segment seconds in title only, RecalibrateControl run completion has no live region.
